candidates.locator: Page: 16, Section: part_i, Part II §3 REPORTING
candidates.exact_span: For any test which fails, is considered invalid, or which is terminated early for any reason, the full report must be submitted for agency review.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether failed, invalid, or early-terminated tests count as documented evidence versus absent monitoring affects how missing-evidence semantics are classified when no ordinary DMR numeric result exists.

candidates.locator: Page: 16, Section: part_i, Part II §3 REPORTING
candidates.exact_span: A valid test for each species must be reported during each reporting period specified in PART I of this permit unless the permittee is performing a TRE which may increase the frequency of testing and reporting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'valid test,' 'each species,' reporting-period linkage to PART I, and the TRE exception changes which biomonitoring obligations were required in FY2025 and whether missing DMR results reflect non-requirement, inadequate evidence, or unresolved applicability.

candidates.locator: Page: 16, Section: part_i, Part II §3 REPORTING
candidates.exact_span: One set of biomonitoring data for each species is to be recorded on the DMR for each reporting period. Additional results are reported under the retest codes below.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which single result set is the operative reported measurement per species/period, and whether retests are supplemental rather than primary, affects limit comparisons, monitoring-obligation satisfaction, and classification of missing versus retest-reported data.

candidates.locator: Page: 16, Section: part_i, Part II §3 REPORTING
candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall submit the results of each valid toxicity test on the subsequent monthly DMR for that reporting period as follows below. Submit retest information clearly marked as such with the following month's DMR. Only results of valid tests are to be reported on the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Timing rules (subsequent monthly DMR vs following month for retests) and the valid-test-only DMR rule determine which reported measurements are available for limit comparison, which reporting obligations apply, and whether invalid or untimely results should be treated as missing evidence or documented non-reportable states.

candidates.locator: Page: 16, Section: part_i, Part II §3 REPORTING
candidates.exact_span: Enter a "1" if the No Observed Effect Concentration (NOEC) for survival is less than the critical dilution, otherwise enter a "0".
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this coded 1/0 entry is an enforceable compliance determination against critical dilution, versus report-only coding, changes exceedance analysis for Purpose A; it also defines a required reported parameter for Purpose B.

candidates.locator: Page: 16, Section: part_i, Part II §3 REPORTING
candidates.exact_span: Report the NOEC value for survival
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the reported NOEC as a measurement subject to numeric limit comparison, or as informational report-only data, changes whether Purpose A performs an exceedance evaluation.

candidates.locator: Page: 16, Section: part_i, Part II §3 REPORTING
candidates.exact_span: Report the highest (critical dilution or control) Coefficient of Variation
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this CV value is an enforceable numeric limit, a report-only QA metric, or a conditional reporting field affects applicable-limit identification and whether its absence triggers a monitoring obligation under Purpose B.

candidates.locator: Page: 16, Section: part_i, Part II §3 REPORTING
candidates.exact_span: (If required) Retest 1 – Enter a "1" if the NOEC for survival is less than the critical dilution, otherwise enter "0".
candidates.computation_change_reason: When a retest is 'required' and whether retest 1 outcomes supersede or supplement the primary DMR entry affects which measurement/limit pair is evaluated (A), whether additional monitoring was obligatory (B), and how to classify periods with only primary, only retest, or no reported valid results (C).

candidates.locator: Page: 16, Section: part_i, Part II §3 REPORTING
candidates.exact_span: (If required) Retest 2- Enter a "1" if the NOEC for survival is less than the critical dilution, otherwise enter "0".
candidates.computation_change_reason: Same as Retest 1: conditional retest triggering and retest-sequence precedence change limit comparisons, obligation counts, and missing-evidence classification when multiple retest slots may apply.

candidates.locator: Page: 16, Section: part_i, Part II §3 REPORTING
candidates.exact_span: (If required) Retest 3- Enter a "1" if the NOEC for survival is less than the critical dilution, otherwise enter "0".
candidates.computation_change_reason: Same as Retest 1 and 2: the third retest slot's conditional requirement and reported 1/0 coding affect which toxicity result is operative for compliance, whether further monitoring was mandated, and how incomplete retest series are semantically classified.
